title: WPPIL/39/2017 of Sarop Singh Punder Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (P.I.L.) No.39 of 2017
Sarop Singh Punder .....Petitioner

Versus
State of Uttarakhand & Others .......Respondents
Mr. Gopal K. Verma, Advocate for the appellant
Mr. Pradeep Joshi, Standing Counsel for the State/respondent nos.1 to 4
Mr. Ravi Babulkar, Advocate for respondent no.5
Mr. Shiv Pandey, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Aman Rab, Advocate for the
respondent nos.6 & 7
Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.

Dated: 08.05.2017
K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)
Petitioner has approached this Court seeking
the following reliefs:
"a- Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of certiorari quashing the government
order for allotment dated 06.05.2015
(Annexure-5).
b- Issue a writ of mandamus or any other
appropriate writ/direction to the respondents
not to construct trenching ground nearby Holy
River Ganga in village Khadri Kharak Maf,
Tehsil Rishikesh District Dehradun."
2. Briefly put, the case of the petitioner is as
follows:
The Chairman, Nagar Palika Parishad,
Rishikesh sent a proposal/letter dated 25.08.2009 to the

2
State Government to provide 10 acres of land for
disposal of solid waste coming out from the city of
Rishikesh. Sub Divisional Magistrate, Rishikesh sent a
proposal for allotment of 2 hectares land of Village
Khadri Kharak Maf, Tehsil Rishikesh by communication
dated 17.02.2009. The Tehsildar, Rishikesh sent a
proposal for trenching ground and further recommended
allotment of 10 acres land, belonging to khasra no.22 of
Gram Sabha of Village Khadri Kharak Maf, Tehsil
Rishikesh. The Tehsildar suggested for prior permission
from the State Pollution Control Board as well as
Uttarakhand Remote Sensing Agency. The State
Government, by ignoring the recommendation made by
the revenue authorities and without prior sanction,
issued Government Order dated 06.05.2015 (impugned
order), allotting 10 acres of land of Gram Sabha, free of
cost, for trenching ground for disposal of solid waste in
favour of Urban Development Department.
3. It is stated that, on 23.06.2015, the Additional
District Magistrate, Dehradun directed the Sub
Divisional Magistrate, Rishikesh for mutation. The
Executive Officer, on 10.06.2015, requested the District
Magistrate Dehradun to transfer the said 10 acres land
to Nagar Palika Parishad Rishikesh. Petitioner has made
representations on various dates in July and September,
2015. On 26.09.2015, a meeting was called by the Land
Management Committee of Village Khadri Kharak Maf, in
which it was resolved that the land belongs to Gram
Sabha and it will not be handed over for construction of
trenching ground at any cost. Petitioner represented on
28.09.2015 before the Chief Minister pointing out that

3
the proposed site is just nearby the Holy River Ganga. It
is, thereafter, that the petitioner had approached this
Court earlier. Annexure-1 judgment was issued, which
reads as follows:
"Petitioner challenges Government Order dated
06.05.2015 (Annexure-3). He also seeks a
direction to respondent nos.4 not to construct
trenching ground on the bank of holy river Ganga,
on the land belonging to Gram Samaj of Village
Khadri Kharak Maf Tehsil Rishikesh, District
Dehradun.
2. Briefly put, the case of the petitioner is as
follows:
By the impugned order, the State
Government has made over 10 acres of land of the
4th respondent for construction of the trenching
ground. It is contended, inter alia, that this site is
actually located very near to holy river Ganga and
he seeks to substantiate it with certain
photographs.
3. Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the
4th respondent would submit that search for site
for trenching ground began in 2009 and the
Government has allotted the land and the land
has been got mutated in the name of the 4th
respondent. That is all that has happened.
According to him, further various procedures will
have to be undergone before the land is used as a
trenching ground. They have to get various
permission under various laws. According to him,
in short, this petition is premature.
4. We would think that at this juncture, we
need not consider the issue raised by the
petitioner. We record the stand of the 4th
respondent that all that has happened is that the
land (10 acres) has been got mutated in his name.
It will have to take steps for establishing it as a
trenching ground since various procedures in law
would have to be undergone. We leave it open to
the petitioner to raise all his contentions before
the statutory Authorities. We further leave open
to the petitioner if he is ultimately aggrieved to
seek the same reliefs, which he has sought in the
writ petition by filling a fresh writ petition.

4
Leaving open the contention of the petitioner, the
writ petition is dismissed."

4. It is stated that, on 01.12.2015 and
02.12.2015, petitioner filed representations following the
judgment of this Court. Further, petitioner got
information from Nagar Palika Parishad Rishikesh
regarding issuance of No Objection Certificate by Gram
Sabha Khadri Kharak Maf, Tehsil Rishikesh. Petitioner
was supplied with further information on 13.10.2016 by
the Nagar Palika Parishad. It appears that the
information was that they have no record of No Objection
Certificate issued by the Village Panchayat. Petitioner
made another representation on 06.01.2017 to the
District Magistrate, Dehradun and is before us seeking
the reliefs, which we have already adverted to.
5. We have heard Mr. Gopal K. Verma, learned
counsel for the petitioner, Mr. Pradeep Joshi, Standing
Counsel for the State, Mr. Ravi Babulkar, learned
counsel for respondent no.5-Nagar Palika Parishad,
Rishikesh and Mr. Shiv Pandey, Advocate holding brief of
Mr. Aman Rab, learned counsel for respondent nos.6
and 7.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that land has been allotted and, therefore, even
though he moved representation, no action has been
taken.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent
no.5 and also learned counsel for respondent nos.6 & 7

5
would submit that, as of now, they have not applied for
establishment of the trenching ground. Learned counsel
for Nagar Palika Parishad would submit that various
stages are there and there is also provision for public
hearing under The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
8. We do not see any justification for the
petitioner to approach this Court again at this stage. We
had already left open the right of the petitioner to
approach the Court in the earlier round of litigation. We
see no substantial change in the position. We close this
matter. However, we leave it open to the petitioner to
raise all the contentions before the Statutory Authorities
and we further leave it open to the petitioner, if he is
ultimately aggrieved, to seek the same reliefs, which he
has sought in the writ petition by filing a fresh writ
petition. Leaving open all the contentions of the
petitioner, the writ petition is disposed of.
